_comment: Storm Charge tuning. Portable balance data - no Roblox types in here. RETUNED 2026-10-26 to Chris's curve, replacing the handoff's 8-minutes-to-first-threshold anchor, which left a dark crew with no escalation inside any run it would actually play. One active lantern still raises the meter 2.5x - that anchor is untouched. One charge unit is one second of darkness.

lantern._comment: multiplier = 1 + perLanternBonus * (1 - diminishingDecay^activeLanterns) / (1 - diminishingDecay). One lantern = 2.5x, per the handoff, and the diminishing curve preserves that anchor exactly. Each further lantern adds less than the one before it but never nothing, so no keeper's light is free.
lantern._curveChoice: Chris, 2026-10-27: 'Switch storm-charge.json to the diminishing curve so no keeper's light is free.' This closes the question docs/VERTICAL-SLICE.md raised - under linearCapped a crew of three at 25% duty met the Warden at 5:31 and a fourth lantern cost nothing, so a four-player run was always the shortest one. Diminishing was already written and tested; only this line moved.
lantern._maxMultiplierNote: INERT while curve is 'diminishing' - that curve self-limits at 4.75x and needs no clamp. Kept because it is the clamp linearCapped would use if the curve were ever switched back, and because the balance test still checks a cap can never sit below the one-lantern anchor.

_curveOptions.linearCapped: 1 + bonus*n, hard-clamped at maxMultiplier. Simple, but every lantern past the clamp is free: three (5.5x) and four (7x) both clamp to 5.0. Was the default until 2026-10-27.
_curveOptions.diminishing: ACTIVE. 1 + bonus*(1-decay^n)/(1-decay). Each extra lantern adds less than the last but never nothing, so no player's light is free. Preserves the locked 2.5x one-lantern anchor exactly and self-limits near 4.75x with the values below - no clamp needed.

lantern._decayNote: Only used when curve is 'diminishing'. 0.6 gives 2.5 / 3.40 / 3.94 / 4.26 for one to four lanterns, asymptote 4.75.

_tuning: Chris, 2026-10-26, for a normal 10-12 minute run. Fully dark: first real pressure around minute 4-5, severe pressure near the final minutes. Lantern used regularly: first pressure around minute 2-3, serious pursuit around minute 6-7. 'So light is never an optional visual effect. It is how you see, find better loot, trigger certain enemies, and make the run escalate faster.'
_derivation: regularUseSeconds assumes the lantern lit about half the time, which is multiplier 1 + 1.5*0.5 = 1.75. At 270 / 480 / 700 that gives dark 4:30 / 8:00 / 11:40 and regular use 2:34 / 4:34 / 6:40, which hits all four of Chris's anchors. oneLanternSeconds is the constant-lit case at 2.5x and is a ceiling nobody plays, not a target. Verified with: node tests/pacing.mjs

run._comment: ADDED 2026-10-28. Run length had no home in the portable layer at all - it lived only in src/shared/Config.luau as the misnamed targetMaxSeconds, which is frozen Luau (row 33) and does not port. So the most-argued-about number in the project was unreadable by the Unreal build. These keys give it one, with the misnaming fixed: a ceiling is not a target, which was the whole of O1.
run._authority: Chris, 2026-10-28, settling O1 outright: 'Make it 10-12 minutes for a standard successful raid. Six minutes is the earliest smart extraction window - not the target run. Retire 6-10 everywhere.' The intended run is the one where 'we pushed our luck, made decisions, and barely got out.'
run._earlyExitNote: His number. Six minutes is a valid survival call, not a target - available when the crew is hurt, carrying something important, or simply has enough. The loading dock pays less for it (data/loot.json payoutModifier 1.0 against the freight lift's 1.6).
run._targetNote: His 10-12 minutes. 660 is the point value for simulation; the band is the design intent and the playtest acceptance range for M4. Row 48 makes one raid one night, so this is the night's window and the run length at once - they stopped being two numbers. tests/balance.test.mjs reads the band from here rather than hardcoding it.
run._hardCeilingNote: DERIVED FROM HIS RULE, not from his number - he should check the arithmetic rather than the intent. He redefined the ceiling as 'enough time for a last-second extraction call and holdout, not extra looting', which retires the old 1200 (20 minutes): at a 720-second target, 1200 permits eight further minutes of looting, which is precisely what the new rule forbids. 720 (top of band) + 30 (the longest extraction commitment, the freight lift's arrivalSeconds) + 8 (extractionCall.sirenSeconds) = 758, rounded up to 780 for slack. A crew at the very end of its night can still call and hold. It cannot shop.
run._supersedes: The 20-minute ceiling in O1's table, which was Chris's own earlier figure for 'a deep Galleria push'. Retired 2026-10-28 by his redefinition of what a ceiling is for. Nothing in the thresholds moves - they were always tuned against the 10-12 reading, which tests/balance.test.mjs has asserted as 600-720 since it was written.

extractionCall._comment: Chris, 2026-10-26: 'Calling extraction: a deliberate loud spike - flare, siren, enemies converging - regardless of current Storm Charge.' Extraction is the climax, not a checkbox: the argument the run builds toward is 'we have enough - call the loud extraction now, defend it, or risk one more store?'
extractionCall._spikeNote: PROPOSED, Chris to set. 180 is three minutes of darkness applied at once, which is deliberately large against thresholds of 270 / 480 / 700 - calling it mid-run should move you a stage, so that calling early and calling late are different decisions. The anchor revive's spike is 120 for comparison.

_dutyProfiles._comment: NAMED 2026-10-28 on Chris's warning, and underscore-prefixed on purpose: these are analysis profiles for tuning and tests, never imported into the engine (see docs/DATA-PIPELINE.md on underscore keys). They exist because 'a normally lit crew' is a phrase, not a number. His warning: 'Otherwise someone later will read normally lit crew as 50%, see a seven-minute Warden, and correctly think the system drifted again.' Each profile carries its own contract, and tests/balance.test.mjs asserts against the names rather than against bare decimals.

normal.label: normal coordinated use
normal.contract: THE BASELINE. Lanterns on about a quarter of the night, used deliberately and shared out. The Warden must land inside warden.arrivalBandSeconds (9-11 minutes) at every crew size. This is the profile every minute target in this file is written against.

bright.label: deliberately bright, risky play
bright.contract: A crew choosing to live brightly. The Warden MAY arrive earlier than its band - light always costs - but must remain survivable and must not invalidate the run, so it may never arrive before run.earlyExitSeconds. At 0.3 sensitivity this is 7:44 to 9:29 depending on crew size.

panic.label: panic / escalation state, not regular play
panic.contract: Everything lit, all night. An explicit emergency rather than a playstyle, and not a configuration the balance is tuned for. The only rule it must obey is Chris's floor: the Warden never arrives at minute four.

_thresholdsNote: TWO entries since 2026-10-28. WardenConverges used to be a third; Chris split it into its own `warden` block below, because the Warden is a late-night escalation rather than the normal consequence of using a lantern. These two keep the building active throughout the run and are unchanged - he was explicit that raising them would push dark crews past the end of the raid again.

thresholds.effect: Patrol routes tighten and Sweepers investigate noise further from their spawn.
All patrols actively hunt. Glimmer scan frequency increases.

warden._comment: SPLIT FROM thresholds, 2026-10-28, on Chris's instruction: 'The Warden is an unkillable, late-night escalation - not the normal consequence of using a lantern. If a reasonably lit crew meets it at 4-8 minutes, the game teaches the wrong lesson: light means activate the unavoidable chase phase early. Players will correctly optimize toward darkness.'
warden._chargeValueNote: Unchanged. A dark crew still meets the Warden at 700s = 11:40, inside the 10-12 minute night, which is exactly where Chris wants it. Raising it would have pushed dark crews past the end of the raid again - which is why he said not to simply raise all thresholds.
warden._arrivalBandNote: Chris's target, 2026-10-28: 'Warden: the closing act, around minutes 9-11 for a normally lit crew.' Held as data so tests/balance.test.mjs and tests/pacing.mjs read it instead of each keeping a copy - the same lesson O1 taught. A fully dark crew is deliberately LATER than this band, near the end of the night, which is the point: darkness buys you the whole raid.
warden._rule: The Warden accrues on its own dampened meter: wardenMultiplier = 1 + lightSensitivity * (lanternMultiplier - 1). At 0 the Warden ignores light entirely and always arrives at 11:40; at 1 it behaves exactly as the old third threshold did. 0.4 means a lit crew still summons it earlier - light always costs - but using a lantern is no longer a button that starts a six-minute chase.
warden._derivation: DERIVED to hit Chris's stated arrival targets, not chosen. He set: Warden at 9-11 minutes for a normally lit crew, 11-12 fully dark, four players somewhat earlier than solo but never minute four. 0.4 was tried first and put crews of three and four at 8:37-8:55, under his floor. At 0.3 every crew at 25% duty lands inside the band - solo 10:27, two 9:44, three 9:28, four 9:21 - with four players still earlier than solo, fully dark 11:39 at every crew size, and the worst case anywhere (four lanterns lit 100% of the night, the corner nobody plays) at 5:53, which clears his never-minute-four line. Verify with: node tests/pacing.mjs
warden.effect: The Warden spawns at the rooftop stage and converges on the crew's brightest position.
warden._keepsRow7: Still unkillable and still drops nothing (row 7). This changes when it arrives, never what it is.

anchorRevive._comment: Solo rule: one self-revive per run, paid for with light.
anchorRevive._soloOnlyNote: LOCKED by the handoff: "Solo players receive one Anchor Revive per run." It exists so a lone Lightkeeper is not hard-wiped on a first knockdown. Granting it to a crew breaks the other half of the same rule - a whole crew down must wipe rather than wait indefinitely for someone to press R. Chris later locked the harsher haul rule: a wipe without extraction loses all run loot. Do not set false without changing the handoff first.
